events.text: The Seattle site began brewing beer.
Rainier was founded.
The brewery was closed by Pabst.
The green T was removed by Tullys.
A red neon replica R returned to the top of the brewery.
A.B. Rabbeson opened Washington Brewery.
Rabbeson renamed his brewery Seattle Brewery.
The brewery launched Rainier beer.
John Kopp and Andrew Hemrich founded Seattle Brewing and Malting.
Rabbeson sold his brewery and the Rainier brand to Kopp and Hemrich.
Kopp and Hemrich produced Rainier beer in Washington until the state enacted its own prohibition.
Kopp and Hemrich brewed Rainier beer in San Francisco until the 18th amendment was ratified.
The brewery began brewing Rainier.
The brewery began operating under names including Sicks Seattle Brewing and Malting and Sicks Rainier Brewing Company.
The period of using names such as Sicks Seattle Brewing and Malting and Sicks Rainier Brewing Company ended.
The branch brewery in Spokane closed.
Rainier began packaging beer in the decorative Jubilee Series cans.
Rainier stopped packaging beer in the Jubilee Series cans.
Rainier marketed a set of Christmas cans.
Rainier marketed a set of Christmas cans again.
Rainier and other brands began losing market share to major national brands.
Rainier and other brands began losing market share to major national brands.
Rainier ran a number of memorable television ads in the Pacific Northwest.
A commercial featuring a motorcycle revving Rainier Beer was notable.
A commercial featuring a motorcycle revving Rainier Beer was notable.
The brewery was sold to G. Heileman Brewing Company.
Pabst Brewing Company closed the brewery.
The Olympia Brewing Company closed.
Sleeman Breweries acquired Stroh Canada which owned the Canadian rights to Rainier.
Rainier was awarded a silver medal by the Great American Beer Festival for Best American Light Lager.
Rainier was awarded a gold medal by the Great American Beer Festival for Best American-Style Lager.

The red Rainier R logo dates back to the 1900s.
The company adopted the current R logo since the 1950s.
A large red neon R logo sign was created and placed atop the brewery.
Tullys leased the brewery and replaced the iconic R with a green neon Tullys T sign.
Tullys decided to replace the green T with a replica of the red R sign.
The green T sign was removed.
The new red R sign was installed.
The Rainier Brewery R sign was restored.
Rainier beer is consumed by characters in the film Stand By Me.
The band Mudhoney is photographed with cans of Rainier Beer.
Rainier beer appears in the film Twilight.
A black bear consumes 36 cans of Rainier beer in Baker Lake, Washington.
The main character of the television series Longmire exclusively drinks Rainier beer.
